1. No belt loops.  This significantly limits the versatility, as you need to wear your shirt out to cover the waistband.  For $40 the manufacturer could have included belt loops, and I can't see that there would be any downside to doing so.

3. The fabric has a silvery sheen at a shallow angle, maybe due to the spandex.  Because of the sheen it doesn't really look like denim.
4. There are strange, faint, horizontal stripes in the front below the pockets.  What's up with that?  The manufacturer must have done it deliberately, but whatever their intent was, I don't like it.
5. The waist drawstring (bias tape) has absolutely no stretch, so the pants can't be pulled off and on quickly.  I replaced the drawstring with 1/2" elastic, and that works better for me.
6. No choice of inseam length.  I'm just lucky that 32" is my size.

Lack of a functional fly could be considered a pro or con.  It is inconvenient, but no worse than track suit pants.  And a zipper fly would compromise  the soft, stretchy comfort.

Despite the longer list of cons than pros, I'm giving it 4 stars because of the comfort.  Most of the cons could be fixed if the company would pay attention to customer feedback.

Instead of dropping $58,000 on the gen, this SO&CO homage to the 50th Anniversary Rolex Daytona watch is an acceptable substitute. It's case, bezel, bracelet, and crystal are all top notch; the watch itself is heavy (@ 176 grams) and does not feel cheap. Furthermore, it indeed is water resistance to a respectable 100m or 330 feet.  I know because I have several of these watches and have had them in the swimming pool with no problems. This watch, along with the other SO&CO watches are worth exploring and having. You won't regret it.

This is a very nice watch, especially for the price. A very attractive watch. It is quite heavy with a substantial feel. I had to remove 3 links for it to fit my wrist, which was not easy. I used a very small miniature screwdriver and a hammer to tap out the link connecting pins. I have since discovered that there is a special tool for this purpose. (Perhaps I should get one...) Once adjusted, it is very comfortable. The band has a double-latch clasp that is very secure, yet thin and comfortable. The hour and minute hands glow in the dark, but that's all. Being a diver's watch, the crown must be unscrewed in order to set the time. The upper and lower buttons can be pushed to set the day and date respectively. The dial at the 9 o'clock position indicates 24 hour ime.  Overall, I'm very pleased with the watch and enjoy wearing it.  And it looks just like a $60K Rolex!

**Pros:
1.  Quality - The swimsuit is made well.  I do not think you will have too much of an issue with the netting portion falling apart since it was made fairly well.
2.  Design - I like the design of the swimsuit.  Since there is netting, it does somewhat mask any belly imperfections.  There is also cute button detail long the side of the suit.  The swimsuit also comes with straps so you can turn it to a halter or use it for more security.
3.  Packaging -  The suit comes in a nice plastic container.  I would recommend saving this container for when you go to the pool or the beach and then you can put your wet suit in there after you are done.

**Cons:
1.  Fit - I think if you are smaller chested, this bathing suit would not work.  I am 5'5 and wear about a size 6.  The body of the suit fits me appropriately but not the bust area.  The bust area is molded so you either fill it or not.  For someone that is blessed in the bust area, they probably would love the support.  For me, it does not work.  I thought I ordered a medium but got a large (may have been my mistake).  I would probably would have wanted to try on a medium and that might have fit me better than the large.

In the end, I would have loved to try on the medium.  It may have been a better fit for my bust area.

Very stylish, high quality leather, well made. I can't imagine a more premium wallet, which is good considering the price. It was a little larger than I expected. The full portion could fit a passport and other documents, without the take-out portion you could fit a large phone inside. For the full sized portion you will definitely need to carry it in a coat pocket or a small bag. The take-out portion works pretty well as a stand-alone wallet and also looks great, although the magnetic clasps that are supposed to keep it closed are too flimsy. As another reviewer noted, the slots for the cards are initially very snug. It will take maybe a month or more of regular use to break in the leather so cards slide in and out easily. Same is true for folding the take-out portion: if you have more than 2 cards or a lot of cash, it won't fold in half easily right away. But even though I just got this the leather looks good enough that I'm sure with use it will be easier.

This has been a very useful addition to my bag and wallet collection. I have too many cards and other things to fit into a streamlined wallet - but sometimes I need the streamlined wallet. This one fulfils both, so that I don't have to constantly switch from one wallet to another, I just take the inner wallet when I need a few things , and the whole wallet/bag when I need to have everything with me.  The inner wallet stays in place with magnets when inside the larger piece, and the same magnets help keep the insert wallet together when using it alone. The wallet itself is beautiful and the design is ingenious.  However, credit cards must be slightly smaller in Australia (where the wallet is made) than in the US. The default float setting was perfect for me - I have had absolutely no problems stepping out of these cleats/pedals in traffic whenever I needed to. Unlike a number of people I know who have fallen numerous times with other brands of cleats/pedals, when having to stop. So overall, these have been a great deal and are working really well for me.

Great entry into clipless pedals.  Eventually the pedals wear out and spin too freely, and there is really no way to service them.  But for the price and quality, I can hardly complain.  I have gotten over a thousand miles out of these pedals.

Until purchasing this clipless pedal/shoe combo, I had never used a clipless pedal before (only toe cages).  For those on the fence on whether or not to purchase clipless pedals, I must say, they make a very big difference!  My pedaling has become much smoother and more efficient.  I also feel my entire leg working to pedal.  I'm glad I made the jump.

Regarding this pedal/shoe combo, I like that it comes as a combination and that it is inexpensive.  I followed the advice of other reviewers and purchased a smaller size than I normally wear, based on their US sizing chart.  That is, I typically wear a 9-9.5 size shoe, but purchased the 8.  It fits perfectly.  Although the pedals were simple to install, they required an allen wrench that I didn't have in my 7 piece allen wrench set.  I don't know if that's because I have a deficient set, or the pedals require an uncommon size.

My biggest complaint is that the left shoe has a hole that does not fit the screw.  Both shoes requires that the cleat be screwed in with three screws.  The right shoe is fine.  The left shoe, I can screw in two of the screws, but one of them does not go all the way in.  Since I always place my right foot down first and leave my left foot clipped in when I stop, I haven't had a problem yet.  However, it is noticeably more difficult to unclip my left foot.

All in all, this is a solid entry level pedal/shoe combo.

I've always enjoyed the comfort of Merrell footwear for hiking and walking, but have not previously been a huge fan of their styling. Fortunately they have addressed this issue and I can say I've had many compliments on the style of this shoe. The comfort is still top notch making this model a great all-day walking shoe. There could be a bit more arch support, but these have more than most comparable fashionable sneakers, which usually tend to sacrifice comfort for style. I walk to work every day in New York and these are now my go-to pair of shoes for fair weather. The suede is obviously not ideal for rain or snow, but the few times I have been caught in the rain in these my feet did not get wet, although the shoes did absorb quite a bit of water. Despite what a few other reviewers have said, my feet never overheat in these, even during the hot and humid NYC summers. They are definitely warm, but not uncomfortably so. I expect these will continue to be very cozy when the cooler autumn weather hits.

So far the build quality seems high, with stitching around the entire sole which should increase the lifespan of the shoe and prevent the sole separating from the shoe. The sole is thick and I expect will last quite a while. The white rubber picks up dirt and is nearly impossible to keep in pristine condition, but I personally think that this adds character to the look of the shoes.

Overall I am happy with my purchase and will continue to buy Merrell in the future.

I'm going to start by saying that based on the ring itself, and very cute packaging, this WOULD have been a five star rating if they had ONLY been less... misleading. This is a gorgeous piece of costume jewelry and the amount of labor required to cast and plate the body (yes- PLATE- I will get to that), and cut and set the stones, is worth quite a bit more than twenty bucks.

"Topaz simulated diamond 10k gold filled" with a picture of a blue center stone. Any reasonable person will take that to mean that blue stone is topaz, the side stones are CZ or equivalent, and the body is solid low-karat white gold.
The center stone MAY in fact be topaz; I am not qualified to call that one, but it certainly isn't the color shown in the pictures. It is very nicely cut for a piece in this price range, and shows some color refraction in daylight.
The side stones are for the most part perfectly acceptable, but two that are set in the crown actually have a golden color that once I noticed it, I see at a glance. Again... TWENTY BUCKS. I'm not heartbroken.
Here's why I'm so annoyed. Why can't some Amazon sellers just be honest and say exactly what it is we are buying?
The ad makes it sound like solid cheap white gold. It has a stamp inside the band that says "10K" very clearly. A stamp like that should never, but often does, appear on items with a base metal center. The seller responded to a question by saying 'it's white copper', which is commonly referred to as cupronickel, It's an ideal material for coins and silverware and certainly finds its way into plenty of costume jewellery. That would have been a reasonable material to make a ring like this out of.
I did a quick test on the inside of the ring using a drop of high concentration Nitric acid. If the material were cupronickel, it would have fizzed and turned greenish blue. NOTHING. Well color me surprised, this ring is in fact gold plated.
I scratched through the plating on the inside, having by now decided not to return it because it's so nice looking, and the center is also not 'white copper'. It's plain red copper. A nitric acid test fizzed up and the second picture is of the blue color on a lab wipe. They could have used cupronickel inside, which would have been better as the plating wore off so as not to be so obvious.
NEVER wear this ring to the beach or in any environment where it will be exposed to abrasives.
My last complaint is that I attempted to cancel my order 20 minutes after placing it, and got a message TWO DAYS LATER that it was being shipped. Really?!

Okay now for the good stuff. I ordered this ring to wear with my stainless Invicta watch and the styles complement each other well. The ring is bright and looks and feels much more solid than your average costume jewellery. It IS extremely well put together, even if the material description is questionable. I have a stainless steel ring on order to wear to work, since this one DEFINITELY won't last long at a machine shop, but it will be a fabulous weekend ring.

I have been using this duffel bag from Baosha as an emergency first aid bag for the last month and I am quite impressed with it.

My thoughts about the duffel bag:

01 Well Made - The duffel bag is durable and well made. There is a lot of stitching on this bag and all of it is tight and free of loose threads. The straps are firmly attached to the bag and the snaps and zippers all work as they should. I expect this duffel bag will hold up for a long time.

02 A Good Amount of Space - I am using this duffel bag as my emergency first aid bag and there is plenty of room on the inside for my stuff. Inside the duffel bag I keep my first aid kit, a warm blanket, a flashlight, batteries, paracord, a bag of cotton balls, and bottles of hydrogen peroxide, hand sanitizer, and saline.

There is also a zippered pocket and four zipperless pockets inside of the bag. Two of the zipperless pockets are large enough for phones and other two are suitable for pens and pencils.

On the outside of the duffel bag is a zippered pocket that is large enough for a wallet and keys. There are also a hand sized pockets on each side of the duffel bag that are kept securely shut with snaps.

03 Stylish and Attractive - The duffel bag is made of PU leather but I think it has the look of real leather. Under close inspection, leather aficionados could probably tell it is not real leather but it is still an attractive duffel bag.

04 Odor Free - I was relieved to find this bag is free of the nasty chemical odor that seems to plague cheaper products made of PU leather. This is a huge plus to me and I imagine this would be a plus for anyone that isn't hard of smelling.

05 Versatile - I like having the option to either carry the bag by the handles or use the included strap and sling it over my shoulder.

06 Unisex - The look of this duffel bag may be geared towards men but it is also suitable for women.

Ordered an M and an XL because I understood that these would shrink and knew ahead of time that I would be "working" on these to make them long enough to tuck your feet into.

Washed both gowns in warm/cold and dried warm/hot to get the most shrinkage before giving either as a gift.
The length drew up 2-3 inches from the length out of the package.
IMO, no excessive (for 100% cotton flannel) shrinkage otherwise, but you want nightgowns to be "roomy," so purchase accordingly.
I was skeptical about the eyelet being 100% cotton, but I think it may be. It looks good for it. I cannot speak for the thread that is a part of the eyelet, but it seems too shiny for cotton thread. The eyelet is nicer than expected.

The medium gown's "sweep" (hemline) measures 54" across (after laundering), and the XL is about three inches wider (about 57"). Compare this with the sweep of your favorite gown. To small a sweep gives you a "hobble" gown and you can trip yourself up in it.

The XL's laundered length is about an inch (yes, 1" only) longer than the Medium's laundered length, which is 47" from the nape of the neck to the hem at the back.

I am pleased with the weight of these and the fabric so far.

To create the length I need for these gifts, I am adding a ruffle in a solid flannel (prelaundered to shrink the fabric before cutting), using a 13" ruffle on the M for a 5'8" lady and a 9" ruffle on the slightly longer XL for a 5'5" lady.

The ruffle will be hemmed in the fabric of the original gown.

If you decide to go this far to make this gown work, you may want to see Mark Montano's "Make your Mark" sewing video "How to add a ruffle hem" for the principle of adding the ruffle and also have a look at "3 ways to gather" from Threads for the "hard" part. These are both on youtube. I prefer two gathering lines for prettier gathers, the second to sit virtually at the final seam line. For that method, the second video will be helpful.
